domainTools.description: Include domain-matched tools for result URLs. Defaults to true when Alexandria is combined with web, news or images; semantic-only search leaves domain matching off.

highlights.description: Return query-relevant page excerpts for web and news results when available (default). Highlights appear in web `description` and news `snippet`; otherwise, original snippets are returned. Set to false to keep the original search snippets.

includeDomains.description: Hostnames to restrict results to. Mutually exclusive with excludeDomains.

excludeDomains.description: Hostnames to leave out of results. Mutually exclusive with includeDomains.

sources.description: Search sources; authenticated sessions default to web + alexandria, keyless sessions to web only. Authenticated searches always add alexandria to the sources, so sources: ["web"] also returns providers; domainTools: false turns off website-matched tools only. enterprise zdr or anon searches do not add it. Use ["alexandria"] alone for provider discovery without web results.

categories.description: Limit results to specific source types. `research` restricts ordinary web results to research-affiliated websites and returns page snippets, which is separate from the `firecrawl_research_*` tools that search paper abstracts and full text across biomedical (PubMed, bioRxiv, medRxiv) and arXiv literature; `pdf` searches PDF results; `developer` searches an index built for coding agents over public repositories, GitHub issues, merged pull requests, repository READMEs, and code documentation; `gov` searches the Government Index of US federal, state, and local legal and regulatory sources, the index behind firecrawl_gov_search, and cannot be combined with other categories; gov hits can include historical versions, bill text, agency guidance, and third-party reproductions, so verify the issuer, jurisdiction, enacted/effective status, and version before citing current governing law, clarify a missing jurisdiction or ambiguous as-of date, and use general search for non-US questions or missing coverage (no hits does not establish that no applicable law exists). `developer` and `gov` return hits in `data.web` with `category` set to their name; the other categories also filter `data.web`.

objective.description: The user's underlying goal for this call, in one sentence: what they are ultimately trying to accomplish, not a restatement of the URL or query. Reuse it across related calls. Avoid sensitive information.

definition.name: mcp__claude_ai_Firecrawl__firecrawl_search_feedback
definition.description:
Records schema-validated quality feedback for a prior `firecrawl_search` UUID `searchId`. A `good` rating requires a valuable result or a valuable source, `partial` either of those or at least one `missingContent` entry, and `bad` at least one `missingContent` entry or a query suggestion; caps are 50 `valuableResults`, 50 `valuableSources`, and 20 `missingContent` entries.

Eligibility is limited to successful searches within the feedback age window. The record is idempotent per search ID. Eligible first feedback for a search can refund 1 credit; refunds are subject to the team's daily cap. The response reports whether a refund was applied, along with submission and daily-cap status.

Mark useful returned results in `valuableResults` as `{"source", "position"}` copied off the result. Groups are numbered from 1 independently, so `{"source":"web","position":1}` and `{"source":"news","position":1}` are different results. Be exhaustive — results you do not list are treated as not useful. Reserve `valuableSources` for useful URLs that were NOT among the returned results; never report one result in both fields.

valuableResults.description: Every result that was actually useful, copied from the `source` and `position` stamped on each result. Each group is numbered from 1 independently, so the source is required — `{"source":"web","position":1}` and `{"source":"news","position":1}` are different results. Be exhaustive — unlisted results are treated as not useful. Do not also list the same results in valuableSources.

missingContent.description: Array of specific pieces of content the agent expected to find but did not. One entry per distinct topic. Each entry has a short `topic` and optional longer `description`.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

A workflow size guideline is configured for this session: small — keep workflows under 5 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale.

"""Innermost-scope lookup by byte offset, shared by the language slices."""

from __future__ import annotations

import bisect


class Nesting:
    """The innermost scope whose body holds a byte, in O(log depth).

    Scope 0 is the whole file. Bodies nest, so the innermost scope holding a byte is an
    ancestor-or-self of the last body starting at or before it, and ancestors' bodies
    end no earlier. ``jumps[k][j]`` is the 2**j-th ancestor of ``k``: skipping the
    ancestors that end at or before the byte takes O(log depth), where one parent at
    a time is quadratic after a deep nest.
    """

    def __init__(self, size: int) -> None:
        self.bodies: list[tuple[int, int]] = []  # (body start, scope), sorted
        self.ends = [size]
        self.parents = [0]
        self.jumps: list[list[int]] = [[]]

    def add(self, parent: int, body: tuple[int, int]) -> None:
        own = len(self.ends)
        up = [parent]
        while len(self.jumps[up[-1]]) >= len(up):
            up.append(self.jumps[up[-1]][len(up) - 1])
        self.ends.append(body[1])
        self.parents.append(parent)
        self.jumps.append(up)
        bisect.insort(self.bodies, (body[0], own))

    def scope_at(self, at: int) -> int:
        i = bisect.bisect_right(self.bodies, (at, len(self.ends))) - 1
        k = self.bodies[i][1] if i >= 0 else 0
        if not k or at < self.ends[k]:
            return k
        for j in range(len(self.jumps[k]) - 1, -1, -1):
            if j < len(self.jumps[k]) and (up := self.jumps[k][j]) and self.ends[up] <= at:
                k = up
        return self.parents[k]
    def member(self, node: Node) -> None:
        data, parent = self.data, self.scope_at(node.start_byte)
        name = node.child_by_field_name("name")
        if name is None or not self._is_type(parent):
            return  # a member of a local or anonymous class: part of that scope
        body = node.child_by_field_name("body")
        params = [
            p
            for p in _named(node.child_by_field_name("parameters"))
            if p.type in ("formal_parameter", "spread_parameter")
        ]
        method = node.type in ("method_declaration", "annotation_type_element_declaration")
        decl = Decl(
            "method" if method else "constructor",
            _text(data, name),
            *_span(node),
            _signature(data, node, body.start_byte if body else node.end_byte),
            len(params),
            any(p.type == "spread_parameter" for p in params),
            method
            and any(
                _dotted(data, a.child_by_field_name("name")).rpartition(".")[2] in TEST_ANNOTATIONS
                for a in _annotations(node)
            ),
        )
        self._open(parent, Scope(parent, decl), node)

    def anonymous(self, body: Node, base: str | None) -> None:
        parent = self.scope_at(body.start_byte)
        supers = [Use(base, body.start_byte, body.start_byte)] if base else []
        self._open(parent, Scope(parent, None, supers), body)

    def bind(self, name: Node | None, kind: str | None) -> None:
        if name is None:
            return
        bound, text = self.scopes[self.scope_at(name.start_byte)].bound, _text(self.data, name)
        bound[text] = kind if bound.get(text, kind) == kind else None

    def variable(self, node: Node) -> None:
        data = self.data
        if node.type in ("type_pattern", "record_pattern_component"):
            parts = _named(node)
            if len(parts) == 2 and parts[1].type == "identifier":
                self.bind(parts[1], type_name(data, parts[0]))
            return
        name = node.child_by_field_name("name")
        if node.type == "catch_formal_parameter":
            caught = next((c for c in node.named_children if c.type == "catch_type"), None)
            types = _named(caught)
            self.bind(name, type_name(data, types[0]) if len(types) == 1 else None)
            return
        kind = node.child_by_field_name("right" if node.type == "instanceof_expression" else "type")
        array = node.child_by_field_name("dimensions") is not None
        self.bind(name, None if array else type_name(data, kind))

    def variables(self, node: Node) -> None:
        kind = type_name(self.data, node.child_by_field_name("type"))
        for declarator in node.children_by_field_name("declarator"):
            array = declarator.child_by_field_name("dimensions") is not None
            self.bind(declarator.child_by_field_name("name"), None if array else kind)

    def call(self, node: Node) -> None:
        data, name = self.data, node.child_by_field_name("name")
        receiver = node.child_by_field_name("object")
        if name is None:
            return
        if receiver is None:
            form = ""
        elif receiver.type in ("this", "super", "identifier") or _path(receiver):
            form = _dotted(data, receiver) + "."
        else:
            return  # a call on an expression's value: needs its type
        arity = len(_named(node.child_by_field_name("arguments")))
        self.use(Call(form + _text(data, name), node.start_byte, name.end_byte, arity))

    def new(self, node: Node) -> None:
        kind = node.child_by_field_name("type")
        if kind is None or not node.children or node.children[0].type != "new":
            return  # ``outer.new Inner()``: needs the outer value's type
        base = type_name(self.data, kind)
        if base is not None:
            self.created.add(kind.start_byte)
            arity = len(_named(node.child_by_field_name("arguments")))
            self.use(Call(f"new {base}", node.start_byte, kind.end_byte, arity))

    def use(self, call: Call) -> None:
        self.scopes[self.scope_at(call.start)].calls.append(call)


def _body(node: Node, what: str) -> Node:
    """The node a scope spans: an anonymous class's body, else the declaration."""
    if what != "anonymous":
        return node
    return next(c for c in reversed(node.named_children) if c.type == "class_body")


def parse(data: bytes) -> Parsed | str:
    """Syntax facts, or the reason the file is unsupported."""
    try:
        data.decode("utf-8")
    except UnicodeDecodeError:
        return "Java source is not UTF-8"
    root = Parser(LANGUAGE).parse(data).root_node
    if too_deep(root):
        return TOO_DEEP

_NAME = r"(?!\d)[\w$]+"
_DOTTED = re.compile(rf"{_NAME}(?:\.{_NAME})*")


def _sound(parsed: Parsed, size: int) -> bool:
    """What ``parse`` guarantees: in-bounds spans, typed values, a scope tree whose
    parents precede their children, identifier and dotted names, so identities stay
    unique and lookups well-formed."""

    def span(a: Any, b: Any) -> bool:
        return type(a) is int and type(b) is int and 0 <= a <= b <= size

    def dotted(v: Any) -> bool:
        return type(v) is str and _DOTTED.fullmatch(v) is not None

    def texts(*values: Any) -> bool:
        return all(type(v) is str for v in values)

    scopes = parsed.scopes
    if not scopes or scopes[0].parent is not None or scopes[0].decl is not None:
        return False
    for k, s in enumerate(scopes):
        d = s.decl
        if k and not (type(s.parent) is int and 0 <= s.parent < k):
            return False
        owner = scopes[s.parent].decl if k and type(s.parent) is int else None
        if d is not None and not (
            k
            and type(d.kind) is str
            and d.kind in KINDS
            # members belong to a declared type; types to one or to the file
            and (owner.kind in TYPE_KINDS if owner else s.parent == 0 and d.kind in TYPE_KINDS)
            and dotted(d.name)
            and "." not in d.name
            and span(d.start, d.end)
            and texts(d.signature)
            and type(d.arity) is int
            and d.arity >= 0
            and {type(d.varargs), type(d.test)} == {bool}
        ):
            return False
        calls = all(
            span(c.start, c.end) and texts(c.name) and type(c.arity) is int for c in s.calls
        )
        if not (
            calls
            and all(span(u.start, u.end) and dotted(u.name) for u in (*s.supers, *s.refs))
            and all(dotted(n) and (t is None or dotted(t)) for n, t in s.bound.items())
            and texts(*s.types)
        ):
            return False
    return (
        (parsed.package == "" or dotted(parsed.package))
        and texts(*parsed.diagnostics)
        and all(
            type(i.static) is bool
            and dotted(i.path)
            and type(i.wildcard) is bool
            and span(i.start, i.end)
            for i in parsed.imports
        )
    )
"""Conservative Java resolution over every ``.java`` file of one capture (docs/java.md).

A package is the files sharing a package declaration, keyed ``module:java:<package>``;
default-package files form one package per directory and no module. Names resolve the
way javac scopes them, over captured source only: enclosing classes and their captured
supertypes, the file's types and single-type imports, the package, then on-demand
imports. A member lookup that reaches a supertype outside the capture, or a local or
anonymous class, is unknown and stays unresolved rather than guessed.

type Site = tuple[int, int]  # (file, scope)
type Package = tuple[str, str]  # ("", package), or (directory, "") for the default package
type Found = list[Site] | None  # None: unknown, so unresolved; []: certainly none
type Variable = tuple[Site, str | None]  # the declaring scope and the declared type

member resolution, tests, cached facts and persisted incremental/full-rebuild equality."""

from __future__ import annotations

import copy
import json
from pathlib import Path

from conftest import REPO, write
from test_go import unresolved
from test_incremental import BAD, _paths, _replace, apply, dump
from test_typescript import derived, resolved

import oxide
from oxide.capture import capture
from oxide.core.indexing import derive, dialect, validate
from oxide.core.languages import java, python

FIXTURE = REPO / "fixtures/java_repo"
MAIN = "src/main/java/com/example/shop"
STORE = f"symbol:{MAIN}/store/Store.java#Store"
CART = f"symbol:{MAIN}/cart/Cart.java#Cart"
TEST = "symbol:src/test/java/com/example/shop/store/StoreTest.java#StoreTest"


def test_fixture_entities_kinds_and_provenance() -> None:
    found = derived(FIXTURE)
    files = {f.path: f for f in found.files}
    assert all(
        assert 0 < bundle.used <= 1024
        assert "static Store open(Mode mode)" in bundle.payload


def test_scoping_is_conservative(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    found = derived(
        write(
            tmp_path,
            {
                "p/T.java": "package p;\nclass T {\n"
                "  static void f() {}\n  void g() {}\n  void g(int a, int b) {}\n"
                "  void shadow(Object T) { T.f(); }\n"  # a variable obscures the type
                "  <U extends T> void generic(U x) { x.g(); }\n"  # a type parameter
                "  void lambda() { java.util.function.Consumer<T> c = t -> t.g(); g(); }\n"
                "  void local() { class L { void q() { g(); } } new L(); }\n"
                "  void arity() { g(1); }\n"  # no g(int): unknown, not g()
                "  void loose() { var t = new T(); t.g(); T[] ts = {}; ts[0].g(); }\n"
                "  void hash() { hashCode(); toString(); }\n"
                "  class In { void g(String s) {} void h() { g(); } }\n"
                "  static class Up extends T { void h() { g(); super.g(); f(); } }\n"
                "  void anon(T o) { new Base() { void r() { o.g(); T.f(); } };\n"
                "    new Runnable() { public void run() { o.g(); } }; }\n"
                "}\n",
                "p/Base.java": "package p;\nclass Base {}\n",
            },
        )
    )
    t = "symbol:p/T.java#T"
    assert not resolved(found, "calls", f"{t}.shadow")
    assert not resolved(found, "calls", f"{t}.generic")
    assert resolved(found, "calls", f"{t}.lambda") == {f"{t}.g"}  # t is untyped: t.g opaque
    assert unresolved(found, "calls", f"{t}.local") == {"new L", "g"}  # a local class
    assert not resolved(found, "calls", f"{t}.arity")
    assert resolved(found, "calls", f"{t}.loose") == {t}  # var and arrays carry no type
    assert unresolved(found, "calls", f"{t}.hash") == {"hashCode", "toString"}
    # The innermost class declaring the name decides, even when no overload fits.
    assert not resolved(found, "calls", f"{t}.In.h")
    assert resolved(found, "calls", f"{t}.Up.h") == {f"{t}.g", f"{t}.f"}  # inherited
    # Inside an anonymous class, a captured base declares no field o; an external one may.
    assert resolved(found, "calls", f"{t}.anon") == {"symbol:p/Base.java#Base", f"{t}.g", f"{t}.f"}
    assert unresolved(found, "calls", f"{t}.anon") == {"new Runnable", "o.g"}


def test_type_lookup_precedence(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    found = derived(
        write(
            tmp_path,
            {
                "a/Box.java": "package a;\npublic class Box { public static class In {} }\n",
                "b/Box.java": "package b;\npublic class Box {}\n",
                "c/Box.java": "package c;\npublic class Box {}\n",
                "c/Use.java": "package c;\nimport a.Box;\nimport b.*;\n"
                "class Use { Box single; a.Box.In nested; }\n",
                "c/Demand.java": "package c;\nimport a.*;\nimport b.*;\n"
                "class Demand { Box pkg; }\n",
                "d/Demand.java": "package d;\nimport a.*;\nimport b.*;\n"
                "class Demand { Box two; }\n",
                "d/Ext.java": "package d;\nimport x.Box;\nclass Ext { Box external; }\n",
                "d/Sub.java": "package d;\nclass Sub extends a.Box { In inherited; }\n",
            },
        )
    )
    refs = {
        e.evidence.path: e.targets
        for e in found.edges
        if e.kind == "references" and e.evidence is not None and e.name == "Box"
    }
    assert resolved(found, "references", "symbol:c/Use.java#Use") == {
        "symbol:a/Box.java#Box",  # a single-type import shadows the package
        "symbol:a/Box.java#Box.In",  # a qualified name
    }
    assert resolved(found, "references", "symbol:c/Demand.java#Demand") == {
        "symbol:c/Box.java#Box"  # the package beats on-demand imports
    }
    assert refs["d/Demand.java"] == ("symbol:a/Box.java#Box", "symbol:b/Box.java#Box")
    assert refs["d/Ext.java"] == ()  # an external single-type import shadows too
    assert resolved(found, "references", "symbol:d/Sub.java#Sub") == {
        "symbol:a/Box.java#Box",
        "symbol:a/Box.java#Box.In",  # an inherited member type
    }

import sys, collections
from oxide.capture import capture
from oxide.core.indexing import derive
from oxide.core.languages import java
snap = capture(sys.argv[1])

def old_open(self, parent, scope, span):
    self.scopes.append(scope); self.nesting.add(parent, java._span(span))

EOF

52	        return path == src.path and char_offset(data[src.path], src.start) <= offset < char_offset(data[src.path], src.end)
53	    if entity and entity.category == "module":
54	        return path in {t.removeprefix("file:") for t in file_modules.get(target, ())}
55	    return False

57

59	    compact = "".join(text.split())
60	    if ")." in compact or "] .".replace(" ", "") in compact:
61	        return "chained call"

75	        ambiguous[kind + ("_hit" if matched else "_miss")] += 1
76	        continue

78	        if kind in ("calls", "references") and oracle_decl:
79	            text=data[at.path][at.start:at.end].decode("utf-8","replace")
80	            unresolved[kind].append((hashlib.sha256(repr(edge).encode()).hexdigest(),edge,oracle_decl,text,unresolved_cause(edge,text)))
81	        continue

83	        no_oracle[kind] += 1

86	    agree=False

89	        if entity and entity.source:
90	            src=entity.source; entity_data=data[src.path]
91	            a,b=char_offset(entity_data,src.start),char_offset(entity_data,src.end)
92	            if decl_path==src.path and a<=decl_char<b: agree=True
93	        elif entity and entity.category=="module":
94	            member_files={t.removeprefix("file:") for t in file_modules.get(target,())}
95	            if decl_path in member_files: agree=True
96	    if agree:
97	        stats[kind]["agree"]+=1
98	    else:
99	        stats[kind]["disagree"]+=1
100	        source=entities.get(edge.source)

103

`-sourcepath` lists every module's `src/main/java`, with two deviations from the brief: it is a symlinked mirror without `module-info.java` (a visible one switches javac to module mode), and it adds gson's `src/main/java-templates` (`GsonBuildConfig`, which OXIDE indexes).

**OXIDE error.** `@JsonAdapter` at `gson/src/test/java/com/google/gson/functional/JsonAdapterAnnotationOnClassesTest.java:221` (on `private static class A`) resolves to the member class `A.JsonAdapter`. javac binds the imported `com.google.gson.annotations.JsonAdapter` (`gson/.../annotations/JsonAdapter.java`). OXIDE looks the annotation up in `A`'s body scope, but the annotations of a class declaration are resolved in its enclosing scope.

content.content:
A lookup that would need one, or that reaches code outside the capture, is unresolved
rather than guessed.

- **Types.** A simple type name resolves in javac's order: type parameters and local
  classes, which are opaque; member types of the enclosing classes, innermost first,
  including types inherited from captured supertypes; then the file's own top-level
  types, single-type imports, types of the same package and on-demand imports. A
  single-type import of something not captured (`import java.util.List;`) still shadows
  the package, so the name is unresolved. Several on-demand imports offering a name
  are ambiguous. A qualified name (`a.b.Box.In`) resolves through its longest captured
  package prefix, or through a type and its member types.
- **Imports.** Each import is an `imports` edge from its file to what it names: the type
  of a single-type import, the package's module (or the type) of an on-demand import, and
  for a static import the methods and member types of that name (every overload, so an
  overloaded name is ambiguous), or the owner type for a field.
- **Methods.** A call `m(...)` resolves to the innermost enclosing class that has a
  member method `m`. Its members are the methods it declares plus those inherited
  through captured supertypes, the nearest declaring type first. Then come
  single-static-imported and static-on-demand-imported methods. Overloads are filtered
  by argument count; varargs methods accept their arity minus one or more. Several
  that fit are ambiguous. `this.m()`, `super.m()`, `Type.m()` and `Type.FIELD.m()`
  resolve against that type. `x.m()` and `this.x.m()` resolve against the declared type
  of `x`: a parameter, local, pattern, resource, catch or loop variable, or a field of
  the enclosing classes or their captured supertypes.
- **Calls** cover method invocations through an identifier, `this`, `super`, a variable,
  a type or `this.field`, and instance creations `new T(...)`, which call the class
  (anonymous class bodies included).
- **References** cover every class or interface type written in a declaration: supertypes,
  fields, parameters, returns, `throws`, locals, casts, type arguments and bounds. They
  also cover annotations (`@Cached`).
- **Conservative locals.** A variable's declared type is kept only when every binding of
  its name in the scope has the same type. A name bound with `var`, a primitive or array
  type, a lambda parameter or several different types is opaque, and so is any name a
  variable shares with a type (javac's variable-obscures-type rule). Calls on opaque
  receivers are unresolved.
- **Unknown members stop the lookup.** If the class holding the call, or one of its
  supertypes, is outside the capture (`extends JPanel`), it may declare the name. So do
  a local or anonymous class body and an enum constant's body. In each case the call is
  unresolved instead of falling through to an outer class's method of the same name.
  The same holds for names every class has implicitly: `Object`'s methods, an enum's
  `values`/`valueOf`/`name`/`ordinal` and the like, and a record's component accessors.

Same-named top-level types in several files of one package (duplicate sources, generated
and handwritten variants) make a reference ambiguous, listing every candidate.

## Not modeled

"""Edges that the declaration-header scope fix changes, on one checkout (measured).

Usage: uv run --locked python annotation-fix-diff.py ROOT OLD_JAVA_PY OLD_JAVA_RESOLVE_PY
Derives ROOT with this checkout, then with the pre-fix slice loaded over the same modules.
"""

import collections
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from oxide.capture import capture
from oxide.core.indexing import derive
from oxide.core.languages import java, java_resolve

snap = capture(sys.argv[1])
new = derive(snap, "evaluation")
for module, path in ((java, sys.argv[2]), (java_resolve, sys.argv[3])):
    exec(compile(Path(path).read_text(), path, "exec"), module.__dict__)
old = derive(snap, "evaluation")
a, b = collections.Counter(old.edges), collections.Counter(new.edges)
gone, added = a - b, b - a
print(Path(sys.argv[1]).name, "edges", sum(a.values()), "removed", sum(gone.values()), "added", sum(added.values()))
for sign, edges in (("-", gone), ("+", added)):
    for e in sorted(edges, key=repr):
        assert e.evidence is not None
        print(f" {sign} {e.kind} {e.source} -> {list(e.targets)} {e.resolution} at {e.evidence.path}:{e.evidence.start}")
EOF
echo ok

cd /home/khoi/Projects/oxide && T=~/Projects/oxide-eval-data/oxide-java-eval/tmp; mkdir -p $T/old && tar -xzf ~/Projects/oxide-eval-data/oxide-java-eval/backup/untracked.tgz -C $T/old --wildcards '*languages/java*.py' && find $T/old -name '*.py' && cat > docs/phase-6/java-v1/verification/annotation-fix-diff.py <<'EOF'
"""Edges that the declaration-header scope fix changes, on one checkout (measured).

Usage: uv run --locked python annotation-fix-diff.py ROOT OLD_JAVA_PY OLD_JAVA_RESOLVE_PY
Derives ROOT with this checkout, then with the pre-fix slice loaded over the same modules.
"""

import collections
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from oxide.capture import capture
from oxide.core.indexing import derive
from oxide.core.languages import java, java_resolve

snap = capture(sys.argv[1])
new = derive(snap, "evaluation")
for module, path in ((java, sys.argv[2]), (java_resolve, sys.argv[3])):
    exec(compile(Path(path).read_text(), path, "exec"), module.__dict__)
old = derive(snap, "evaluation")
a, b = collections.Counter(old.edges), collections.Counter(new.edges)
gone, added = a - b, b - a
print(Path(sys.argv[1]).name, "edges", sum(a.values()), "removed", sum(gone.values()), "added", sum(added.values()))
for sign, edges in (("-", gone), ("+", added)):
    for e in sorted(edges, key=repr):
        assert e.evidence is not None
        print(f" {sign} {e.kind} {e.source} -> {list(e.targets)} {e.resolution} at {e.evidence.path}:{e.evidence.start}")
EOF
echo ok

lines: `score.py` runs `capture` + `derive` (as `eval_java.py audit` does). For each edge, the query position is the last identifier of the evidence, after blanking type arguments, converted from bytes to UTF-16 units. An edge AGREEs when javac's declaration start lies inside a target's span (for a module target, in a file of that package). "Strict" additionally requires the innermost OXIDE symbol containing the declaration to be the target.
+## Precision of resolved edges (after the annotation-scope fix)
| Kind | Agree | Agree (strict) | Disagree | No oracle | Precision |
+Before the fix, the same javac output scored references 5,709 / 1 (0.9998) and overall 14,670 / 1 (0.9999).
+Every other count below is unchanged by the fix.
- **No-oracle reasons:** 3 `calls:error`. In `CircularReferenceTest` lines 57/75/101, javac cannot attribute `assertThrowsStackOverflow(...)` because its argument type comes from absent JUnit.
- **Ambiguous calls:** 2,078. For all 2,078, javac's declaration is one of the candidates (0 in none, final pass).
- **Unresolved, javac in-repo:** 1,079 (calls 134, references 945). By javac element kind: type parameter 874 (OXIDE has no type-parameter entity, by design), METHOD 92, CLASS 73, RECORD 40.

Type parameters dominate the sample. An extra seeded sample of 20 unresolved *calls* (scratch, not the brief's sample) shows outer-class statics called from anonymous bodies (`canonicalize`, `typeToString`, `upperCaseFirstLetter`), local classes and records (`new LocalRecord`, `new NullAdapter`), calls through a static field (`FormattingStyle.PRETTY.withIndent`) and `Object` members (`factory1.equals`).
+## Every disagreement (final pass before the fix: 1; after: 0)

-**OXIDE error.** `@JsonAdapter` at `gson/src/test/java/com/google/gson/functional/JsonAdapterAnnotationOnClassesTest.java:221` (on `private static class A`) resolves to the member class `A.JsonAdapter`. javac binds the imported `com.google.gson.annotations.JsonAdapter` (`gson/.../annotations/JsonAdapter.java`). OXIDE looks the annotation up in `A`'s body scope, but the annotations of a class declaration are resolved in its enclosing scope.

+into an agreement, and it is the only edge of gson that changes ([../verification/annotation-fix-diff.log](../verification/annotation-fix-diff.log)).

**Scorer error (1 class, 8 edges).** For explicit type-argument calls (`gson.<Car>fromJson`), the first pass cut the evidence at the first `<` and queried the receiver `gson`. The fix blanks balanced `<…>` in place, and the rerun places all 8 among the candidates. content.text:
The `@JsonAdapter` bug is fixed and regression-tested. The gson javac oracle now finds **0 disagreements**: 14,671 / 14,671, up from 14,670 / 1. `mise run verify` passes (403 passed, 7 skipped).

**The fix.** Java scopes covered their own annotations, so `@JsonAdapter` on `class A` was looked up inside `A`'s body, where the member class `A.JsonAdapter` shadowed the import. I fixed that in two places:
- **`java.py` (`_Facts._open`):** a declaration's scope now starts after its modifiers, so annotations are resolved in the enclosing scope, as javac does. The resolver still credits those edges to the declaration itself.
- **`java_resolve.py` (`_emit`):** I tested a related case and it had the same bug: `class A extends B { static class B {} }` linked the `extends B` reference to `A.B`. References in `extends`/`implements` now also resolve in the enclosing scope, while the class's own type parameters still apply there.

The facts encoding and version numbers are unchanged, because Java hasn't been released. So the derivation id and the baseline-v15 / typescript-v12 baselines remain valid, and the baseline tests pass.

**Regression coverage.** I added two cases to `test_type_lookup_precedence` in `tests/python/test_java.py`. I confirmed they failed before the fix.

**Effect, measured by deriving each repo with the old and new code:**
- **gson:** exactly one edge changed, the `@JsonAdapter` reference, which now points to the imported annotation.
- **mockito:** no edges changed.
- **The 16 ContextBench repos:** only the 2 gson ones changed, by that same edge. ContextBench metrics and results are byte-identical to before.

**The OpenCode oracle discrepancies are all on its side, not OXIDE's.** I re-ran its own scorer with extra output:
- **The 47 "ambiguous in none" calls have no javac record at all.** Its scorer counts that as a miss:
  - 8 are calls like `gson.<Car>fromJson`, which its scorer cuts at `<`, so it looks up `gson` instead. My first pass had the same bug.
  - 39 are in `test-graal-native-image`, a module it never compiled because it only picks directories that have `src/main/java`.
- **Its 196 edges with no javac result:**
  - 166 are in that skipped module;
  - 24 are static-import members, which javac doesn't attribute;
  - 3 are `GsonBuildConfig` imports, because it left out `java-templates`;
  - 3 are calls javac can't attribute in either run.

  These 193 extra edges it couldn't score are exactly why its agree count is lower.
- On the fixed code, its scorer also gives 14,478 / 14,478 with 0 disagreements.

**Docs updated:**
- `docs/java.md`: the new scoping rule, and the remaining limit below.
- `docs/phase-6/java-v1/README.md`: a new "Fix and re-measurement" section, an explanation of the OpenCode discrepancies, and refreshed tables.
- `docs/phase-6/java-v1/oracle/report.md`.
- New evidence in `docs/phase-6/java-v1/verification/`: `annotation-fix-diff.py` and `opencode-score-dump.py`, each with its `.log`.

I re-ran the real-repo stats and audits for gson and mockito, the oracle score and the ContextBench "after" arm. I did not re-run the benchmark medians, the wheel/sdist smoke test or the ContextBench "before" arm; the README marks them as measured before the fix.

Still not fixed: type-parameter bounds and `permits` clauses can still resolve to the class's own member types (`class A<T extends B> { class B {} }` gives `A.B`). I confirmed this on a small example and listed it in `docs/java.md`.

One risk from not bumping the version: any Java facts cached by the old code would be reused unchanged. Java hasn't been released, so that only affects local eval caches, and I deleted those. Nothing is committed.
